checks.claim: The thorium clock in the heat source, measured to 1%, gives an age range that contains the true age 95% of the time.

Cross-check only: the LNHB and Cheng central ages differ by -0.1 y, because on the atom ratio the U-234 and Th-230 shifts nearly cancel (the research's 103 y is for the activity ratio).

checks.claim: Each heat source started at about 2,400 W; 44,000 years on, the three together still give off 4.9 to 8.7 W. The range rests on two assumptions: whether radon stays in the fuel (its daughters give 3.87 W) and the Cassini-like split of the non-238 plutonium (Pu-239 gives 1.48 W).

checks.expected: design 2,400 W thermal per MHW-RTG at launch (LA-5202: 24 spheres of 100 W); clocks.md 4b estimates about 8 W at 40,000 y, radon retained
checks.tolerance: 2% at launch (nominal design figure); the 44,000-year range is reported, not tested against an independent value
checks.notes: Range assumptions: high = radon retained, so the Ra-226 progeny (Rn-222 to Pb-206, 28.01 MeV per decay, NNDC; gammas counted, an upper bound by about 1.7 MeV) add their heat; low = radon escapes. About 1.5 W comes from Pu-239, which rests on the Cassini split of the non-238 plutonium (an assumption). Alpha decays deposit their full Q value; Pu-241 its mean beta energy. Activities at 44,000 y: U-234 2.55 TBq, Th-230 0.90 TBq, Ra-226 0.86 TBq, Pu-239 1.76 TBq, others 0.037 TBq.

checks.claim: Each Voyager carried about 12.8 kg of plutonium-238; 40,000 years later it has become about 11 kg of uranium-234, 1.1 kg of thorium-230 and 22 g of radium-226.

The Pu-239, Pu-240, Pu-242, U-235, U-236 and Np-237 amounts below rest on that Cassini split and on no uranium impurity in the fuel. At 44,000 y per spacecraft: Pu-239 0.768 kg, Pu-240 3.67 g, Pu-242 23.0 g, Pu-241 none, U-235 1.92 kg, U-236 0.373 kg, Np-237 74 g.

checks.claim: The pulsar age range stays roughly honest even when the real pulsars break the model's assumptions.

checks.claim: Today the map dates itself to about 1971: the Crab (1971.76) and the glitch-corrected Vela pulsar (1971.75) agree on late 1971, and 13 pulsars average 1969.7.

B1642-03 1969.77 (research 1969.77); B1929+10 1969.78 (research 1969.78); B1933+16 1970.19 (research 1970.19); B2016+28 1966.60 (research 1966.6); B2217+47 1969.91 (research 1969.91); B0329+54 1969.76 (research 1969.76); B0525+21 1968.94 (research 1968.94); B0531+21 1971.76 (research 1971.76); B0823+26 1969.14 (research 1969.14); B0950+08 1968.47 (research 1968.47); B0833-45 1972.21 (research 1972.21); B1451-68 1969.52 (research 1969.52); B1727-47 1970.64 (research 1970.64), glitch-corrected 1970.09 (research 1970.09; 6 glitches, sum 3.4246e-6)

checks.notes: F0 and F1 only, except where F2 implies a physical braking index (only the Crab). Glitches added back after the solved epoch up to and including PEPOCH (a glitch within 1 day after PEPOCH counts as at PEPOCH: the ephemeris is the post-glitch fit), iterated until stable. Consistency: glitch-corrected Vela lies 0.01 yr from the Crab, which needs no correction. The research value 1971.77 added back a glitch (#2, MJD 41192) that precedes the date it solved for and omitted the January 2000 glitch at PEPOCH.
